title: A roofing contractor told its insurer it had no employees

beats.text: The roofing contractor told its insurer it had no employees.

visual.sub: One payroll declaration conflicted with another

beats.text: Payroll reports sent to the state told a different story.

visual.kicker: One payroll declaration conflicted with another

beats.text: The employment department had records for five to six employees.

visual.label: One payroll declaration conflicted with another

beats.text: An injured employee then filed a claim with the state insurer.

visual.line: An injured employee filed a claim

beats.text: San Francisco investigators checked the building permits.

visual.kicker: Permits and contract prices supplied independent evidence

beats.text: They compared the insurance declarations with the insurer’s audit records.

visual.kicker: Permits and contract prices supplied independent evidence

beats.text: Property owners provided another check on the numbers.
Investigators compared contract prices with project costs reported to the insurer.

visual.kicker: Permits and contract prices supplied independent evidence

beats.text: Workers at the project sites also spoke with investigators.
Both defendants pleaded guilty to felony insurance premium fraud.
The company manager also admitted trying to dissuade the injured employee.

visual.kicker: The prosecutor reported two premium-fraud pleas

beats.text: The prosecution reports leave the premiums lost unquantified.
They identify no City construction award for these projects.
